transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you into the clinic today?

I'm here because... work has been getting difficult. I'm a nurse, and on the floor, I just... I keep losing my train of thought. It's constant. An IV pump will beep, or someone will ask another nurse a question, or a call light goes off, and... I just completely forget what I was doing or what patient issue I was working on.
When did you first start noticing these difficulties with losing your train of thought?
Um... I suppose it's been a major problem for... almost two years now. That's when I took on some expanded charge-nurse responsibilities at work. So... yeah. Since then.
Looking back to your childhood or school years, did you experience similar difficulties with attention, daydreaming, or staying focused?

Um... yeah, I suppose so. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would write that I was... bright, but careless. I was always losing worksheets. Or I'd just forget to turn my homework in. My mom actually had to sit with me every night... just to keep me on track with it.
Growing up or currently, have you ever felt restless, constantly fidgety, or like you were driven by a motor?
Um... no. Not really. I don't think I've ever really felt... driven by a motor, or anything like that. Just... what I mentioned before.
Aside from these focus issues at work, do you find yourself struggling with persistent, excessive worry about everyday matters that is difficult to control?
Um... no. I wouldn't say that. I mean, work can be stressful, but... I don't really struggle with excessive worrying, or anything like that. It's just the... the losing track of things.
